statement: The 10-K for 2024-12-31 tags the 49,277 Accession Risk Management delayed-draw loan on a second Titan Purchaser member under Automotive, so the Banking, Finance, Insurance & Real Estate subtotal 308,744 finds rows of 259,467; the 10-Q for 2025-03-31 repeats those tags in its comparative schedule. The 10-K also carries the prior-year Second Lien Services: Business subtotal 50,363 on a current-period context. The published row is corrected to Accession Risk Management (row correction of D-099) and carries the Banking industry; the member the filer chose cannot be changed, so the check keeps firing.

The subtotal and its rows sit on members that spell the heading differently, so the check cannot pair them. 2024-06-30: the First Lien Services: Consumer subtotal 328,916 is on the 'Services: Consumer' member, while all its rows but one (CSC Serviceworks, 185) are on members that read 'First Lien Debt Services: FEG, Inc.' and the like, without the word Consumer. 2024-09-30: the Midwest Veterinary second lien loan (35,134) is tagged on a member that begins with the First Lien Services: Consumer heading and then repeats the Second Lien one, which moves three rollups by 35,134 and one by 45,000; and the Metropolis Class A preferred (17,868) is on 'Preferred Equity Consumer' while the subtotal 24,154 is on 'Preferred Equity SERVICES Consumer'. On the page each subtotal equals its rows; the rows are published under the printed lien and industry.

In the 10-Q for 2023-09-30 the filer put three subtotal figures on the wrong members: the Wholesale subtotal (35,982) and the Transportation: Cargo subtotal (65,402) are tagged on each other's members, and the Second Lien Debt section total (219,547) is tagged on the Second Lien Debt Telecommunications member, whose one row is 97. On the page each subtotal equals its rows. No subtotal is published and the published rows equal the filed total, so there is nothing to fix in the data.

The equity rows left without a unit count are two preferred stocks, Xponential Fitness and Accession Risk Management, whose 'Par Amount / Shares' cell the filer prints as a dash and for which it files no share-count or principal fact. Every equity row whose cell prints a figure now publishes it (the column note reads 'Equity investments are recorded as number of shares owned'; 23 counts set from the page in this run). With one or two dash rows among two to six equity rows the check's 70 pct bar is missed in nine quarters. No fix applies: there is no figure on the page to publish.

From the 10-Q for 2025-03-31 Blue Owl Credit Income keeps the '% of Net Assets' column header and prints no percent on its position rows, and tags none. The filed percent goes from 494 rows to 0; the recomputed percent is published for every row.

The fourth-quarter 2022 distribution was a regular 0.65 and a special 0.43 a share, 1.08 against 0.57 to 0.63 in the three quarters before; annualised it is 19.83 pct of net asset value against an income ratio of 10.77. Published is the filed figure.

The yield the check compares is the filer's ratio of net investment income to average net assets (13.88, 13.96, 13.83). The fund is levered: its investments are 225, 215 and 234 pct of net assets in these quarters, so income over net assets sits above the portfolio's weighted coupon (11.80, 11.84, 11.55) by more than the check's two points. Both sides are as filed; the rates of the largest loans were read against the page in the earlier reading.
One loan, Ligado Networks LLC (fair value 1.8M to 4.7M, on non-accrual), is printed and tagged with its original maturity of 11/1/2023 in every later filing. Published is the page.

One row at 2025-09-30 (of 152 tested): the page prints the percent as '0.1 7' across two cells and the filer tagged the first cell, 0.1. Published is the tag; fair value over net assets gives 0.17. No fix applies: percent of net assets is not a field a row correction or a declared value may set.
The sum of percent of net assets, 234.35, is the filer's printed total; the fund borrows and its investments are 188 to 234 pct of net assets in every quarter.

The source row reported as missing is the printed subtotal of the two LJ Perimeter Buyer lines, which the filer tagged on a member spelled like a position. Rule exclude_2025q1_lj_perimeter_subtotal removes it; both lines are published.

The six flagged rows are tranches the filer reports in the Shares/Units column with no principal (the reason of DS-X11-1918712). Five carry a share-count fact. The sixth, JPMMT 2026-ACES1, prints 1,405,613,866 in that column and the filer tagged it with its percent-of-shares concept, so the row publishes neither a count nor a par. Not covered by the accepted entry, whose check requires a share-count fact.

Three Sixth Street Lending Partners lines for which the page prints no par and the filing tags no principal: the second Galileo Parent line at 2023-06-30 (the par is printed once for two lines) and the Cordance Operations loan at 2025-06-30 and 2025-09-30, whose par is printed as a dash (an undrawn line carried at a negative cost and a small positive value). The reason the owner accepted for BCRED Pigments Services (D-152).

Every flagged row (34 in nine quarters, fair value 1 to 162 thousand each) is an undrawn delayed-draw or revolving line. The schedule prints a dash in the Par Amount column and a small fair value, the mark on the commitment; the same figure is in the unfunded-commitments table of the notes. No principal fact is filed on any of the contexts. No fix applies: there is no par on the page to declare.
